question: Does choosing the top-two root action with higher first-half terminal reward retain positive reward difference in independent second-half continuations, within the retained E36 collector?
novel_information: E36 trained shared suffix advantages; this reuses its outcomes to test root preference repeatability without fitting. E175/176 used deterministic greedy continuations, not split independent streams under this stochastic collector. No claim that root-action learning itself is new.
design_history: E36 aggregate outcomes were historically known. The origin-only gate remains failed. Full-suffix outcome-blind coverage found131 families with at leastone observation per prechosen action in each half. This explicitly retrospective diagnostic changes the analysis question; it is not a passed four-forced-pair gate and does not reopen a closed learning recipe.
selection: All256 original families retained. For each family use the earliest full-history node (prefix index then history digest) at which both prechosen highest-probability actions appear in repeats0..3 and4..7. Root selection uses action histories/probabilities, never terminal rewards. No later node search after this test.
teacher: Within repeats0..3 compare mean terminal reward of the two prechosen actions; choose the alternative only for a strict positive difference. Ties choose the collecting-policy top action. Families lacking a qualifying root contribute zero improvement and remain in the denominator.
confirmation: For chosen alternatives, use repeats4..7 mean reward difference alternative minus original top action. Original-top teacher choices contribute zero. Conditional root reward contrast, not natural game wins or public-policy transfer. All negative and zero contrasts retained.
p_value: Exact convolution of each selected root conditional hypergeometric reassignment of second-half binary outcomes across the two action groups, preserving each group count and total wins. Assumes exchangeability under equal action-return distributions; discovery choices remain fixed. Descriptive historical evidence, not selection-adjusted or final acceptance.
interval: 100000 family bootstrap resamples over256 per-family improvement values; seed20260924036; percentile95, descriptive without selection correction. No interval-based tuning.
stop: If original input identities, complete source records or action-history independence fail, invalidate instead of counting losses. If the support gate fails, close this root-preference diagnostic without changing root/action rules, collector, repeat split, thresholds or sample size. If it passes, retain only signal evidence; another separately bounded public-family transfer design is required, no automatic games or learning.
